correctness.rationale: For synchronous open-neighborhood binary majority with ties retained, each outer triangle pair has three types relative to its initial hub: both same, both opposite, mixed. One update makes every pair monochromatic (a mixed pair aligns with the initial hub); every monochromatic pair is thereafter frozen. The hub first reacts to a vs b pair counts and then to b vs m/2, so the second update is fixed. A fixed coloring must have no mixed pairs and at most m/2 opposing pairs. Conditioning on the initial hub gives individual fixed-state basin counts B_m(j)=3^(m−j)+3^j for 2j<m and 3^j at 2j=m; correct handling of a hub tie is essential. Summing basins produces the displayed terminal-blue polynomial, consensus probability (3^m+1)/4^m, and the formula for exactly two rounds; binomial large-number asymptotics yield hub persistence and a 1/2 two-round fraction. A newly implemented synchronous update iterator exhaustively checked all 174760 labelled initial configurations for m=1..8; e.g. m=8 has 326 fixed and 37888 two-round starts. Uniform pair-case proof, not finite extrapolation, covers every integer m>=1.
residual_risks: The retained-tie convention, simultaneous updates, graph topology with triangular peripheral pairs and fair initial-law assumptions are essential; no general tree/windmill-of-other-clique-size result is claimed.
